text: Every one of my apps signs in through one server.
If that server is wrong, every app is wrong.
A sign-in server set up by hand drifts.
And an upgrade can quietly bring back a default sign-in flow, a second, weaker way in.
So nothing here is set up by hand.
One file, over fifteen hundred lines long, describes the whole server.
But a file only says what should be true.
So after every deploy, a check runs inside the server, against the live database.
Only my own sign-in flows exist.
Every app sends people back to an exact secure address.
No app is open to every account.
When all thirty-seven hold, it prints invariants OK.
say: When all thirty-seven hold, it prints: invariants, O K.

text: Now slip one default flow back in.
One lock stays open, and the deploy fails.
